# Finding a Place to Read

原创演示短文、题目与虚构作答。不是雅思真题。

## A

A neighbourhood library opened a reading room beside its entrance, where large windows brought in daylight and helped visitors see the available seats. Although the architects expected the tables beside the front windows to fill first, readers who stayed for more than an hour usually chose the rear corner, from which they could watch the entrance without being seen by everyone coming in. Brief interviews suggested that these readers valued a sense of privacy more than the view of the street.

## B

To understand why a row of chairs near the service desk was rarely used for reading, two staff members observed visitors over six afternoons. What made these chairs unsuitable for reading was not their distance from the books but the irregular noise of the nearby book-return machine. Staff also noticed that visitors waiting to meet friends were happy to use these chairs, since they rarely opened a book.

## C

The library then moved the book-return machine to an alcove away from the reading area. Rather than replace all the furniture, the manager kept the existing chairs and added low screens that could be moved whenever a group needed a larger space. A month later, visitors were staying longer in the area near the service desk, although staff had not yet checked whether the change affected book borrowing.

## 题目

Which paragraph contains the following information? Write A, B or C. You may use a letter more than once.

1. a difference between the seating choice predicted by the designers and the choice made by a particular group of readers

2. a decision to change the arrangement of a space while keeping furniture the library already owned

## 虚构作答与演示答案

| 题号 | 虚构作答 | 本示例答案 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A | A |
| 2 | B | C |
